title: Why Do Humans Tell Stories?
paragraphs: Storytelling is found in every human culture. From bedtime fairy tales to films and video games, stories are one of the main ways we share experiences and entertain one another.

For most of human history, stories were passed on by word of mouth. Around the fire, people told stories about their ancestors, their gods and the world around them. These stories carried history, values and practical knowledge from one generation to the next.

Some stories were later written down. The Epic of Gilgamesh, from ancient Mesopotamia, is among the oldest surviving works of literature. Its themes, such as friendship, loss and the fear of death, still feel familiar thousands of years later.

Psychologists have found that information presented as a story is often easier to remember than a list of facts. Stories also let us imagine the thoughts and feelings of other people, and some research suggests that reading fiction may help us practise empathy.
